query: Consider the following context: Constituent phases and their corresponding phase transformations are important in developing alloys. In that context, which method can be used for control of phase evolution in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni HEAs, and why?

generation.hypothesis: The application of stepwise thermo-mechanical processes can control phase evolution in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni High-Entropy Alloys (HEAs) by inducing specific phase transformations.
generation.material_initial_state: As-cast Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni HEAs with a disordered face-centered cubic (FCC) structure
generation.intervention: Stepwise thermo-mechanical processing with a temperature range of 500-1000°C, strain rate of 10^-3 s^-1, and 5 cycles of hot rolling and annealing
generation.conditions: High vacuum environment, <10^-5 mbar, to prevent oxidation and contamination
generation.structural_mediator: Grain refinement and precipitation of secondary phases, such as sigma (σ) and chi (χ) phases
generation.mechanism: Thermo-mechanical processing induces plastic deformation, which leads to the formation of defects and subsequently promotes the precipitation of secondary phases, thereby controlling phase evolution
generation.predicted_outcome: A 30% increase in the volume fraction of the sigma (σ) phase and a 25% decrease in the grain size, relative to the as-cast state
generation.baseline: As-cast Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni HEAs with a disordered face-centered cubic (FCC) structure
generation.boundary: Temperature range: 500-1000°C, strain rate: 10^-3 s^-1, number of cycles: 5
generation.uncertainty: The exact temperature and strain rate dependencies of the phase transformations are not well established, and the role of other alloying elements on the phase evolution is not fully understood

falsification_experiment.design: Controlled thermo-mechanical processing experiment with varying temperature, strain rate, and number of cycles
measurements: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) for microstructural analysis

falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the volume fraction of the sigma (σ) phase does not increase by at least 20% or the grain size does not decrease by at least 15%, relative to the as-cast state, then the hypothesis is falsified
